world3d.title: AI 3D Immersive Space
world3d.subtitle: Drop in one photo or a short clip and walk around the space it describes. Orbit, pan and zoom a real 3D reconstruction - starting with the subway car below, before you upload anything.
world3d.unsupported: This browser cannot start WebGL2, so the interactive viewer is unavailable. Everything else on this page still works.
world3d.enginePoints: {points} points reconstructed on the local engine
world3d.engineFallback: Local engine unavailable - showing the built-in sample
world3d.uploadTitle: Drop a photo or a clip here
world3d.uploadBody: We lift a 3D space out of a single frame or a short walkthrough, then hand you the scene to inspect from every angle.
world3d.uploadLimits: Up to {image} per image and {video} per clip. With a local engine connected the file goes to that engine on your own machine; otherwise it never leaves your browser.
world3d.errorUnsupportedType: That file type is not supported yet. Use a JPG, PNG or MP4.
world3d.errorTooLarge: That file is too large. Try a smaller image or a shorter clip.
world3d.errorEmpty: That file appears to be empty.
world3d.sourceSampleBody: Subway car - a 20 x 2.8 x 3.5 m preview scan, generated in your browser.
world3d.pipeline1Body: One image or a short clip is decoded locally and sampled into frames - no upload, no queue.
world3d.pipeline2Body: Frames are matched against each other to place a virtual camera in the space they share.
world3d.pipeline3Body: Depth from the solved cameras is fused into a dense cloud of surface samples.
world3d.pipeline4Body: The cloud streams into the viewer as splats, shaded per sample and depth-tested, so it can be inspected in real time.
world3d.noteBody: the reconstruction is simulated locally - every source currently resolves to the subway sample, re-seeded from your file. The viewer, the progress contract and the failure states are production-ready, so wiring in the real reconstruction service replaces one function.
world3d.progressFailedHint: Nothing was reconstructed from this capture. Try a longer walkthrough clip, or more photos with overlapping views.
